conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: A's opening 'First reading' panel states what changed, in whom, and what remains unproven in one above-the-fold block, and it invents nothing: its country caveat says counts 'weren't captured' rather than asserting a value it does not have. B is better structured (a three-act What changed / Where and when / What's not yet answered arc) and materially more accessible, but it asserts two facts the brief does not supply — that every country segment falls under 25 trials, and, in the chart's screen-reader label, that mobile web completion 'trended down across week 28' when only week-level endpoints are given. For a manager whose stated failure mode is a false explanation misdirecting an experiment, the fabrication-free instrument wins. The margin is narrow: A carries its own silent correctness bug in the KPI row.
suspected_unblinding: none — neither build carried a builder signature, framework tell, or comment identifying a treatment. Both desktop.png captures in the packet were taken mid-skeleton and B's evidence screenshots rendered without CSS, so I re-served both sources locally on separate ports and re-captured with a locally-launched Playwright chromium rather than judging from the supplied stills.

unsupported_claims.label: B
unsupported_claims.claim: Asserts as fact that every country segment in week 28 falls under 25 trials. The brief supplies a labeling rule for cuts under 25 trials but never states that all countries are below it; B uses the invented figure to remove the country cut entirely.

unsupported_claims.label: B
unsupported_claims.claim: Chart aria-label states mobile web onboarding completion 'trended down across week 28'. Only week-over-week endpoints (68% to 41%) are supplied; no within-week daily shape exists in the data, and this stronger claim is exposed only to screen-reader users.

unsupported_claims.label: B
unsupported_claims.claim: States 'only Device has numbers loaded for week 28' when switching to the Channel breakdown. Data availability per cut is not supplied; the brief lists acquisition channel as an available cut. Mitigated by being framed as a demo no-data state.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The three KPI cards do not respond to the segment filter, so a manager who filters to Self-serve Desktop reads 'Completed onboarding 54%' beside a chart showing that segment at 70%, with no label marking the KPIs as all-segment.
findings.evidence: Reproduced locally: served A/source on port 8731, selected '#segment-filter' option 'Self-serve · Desktop'; the bar list correctly narrowed to the single Desktop row (73% to 70%) while the KPI block stayed at 14.2% / 54% / 49%. Same desync with the mobile-web option.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Accessibility floor is thin for a filter-driven page: no focus-visible styling, no skip link, 'main' is the only landmark, and no live region announces that filtering changed the results.
findings.evidence: A/source/styles.css contains zero occurrences of focus-visible, prefers-reduced-motion, sr-only, or visually-hidden. DOM probe on the running page returned landmarks ['main'], liveRegions [], skipLink false. Filter changes rewrite the chart with no announcement.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Harness scaffolding leaks into the product surface: the first line of the page reads 'Route: /analytics/trials · viewport tested at 1440x900 and 390px wide', above the page title.
findings.evidence: rv-mine/A/desktop-full.png, top line; also present at 390px in rv-mine/A/mobile-full.png.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The chart legend declares two swatches (Week 27 light, Week 28 dark) but the mobile-web row renders its week-28 portion in red, a third encoding the legend never explains.
findings.evidence: rv-mine/A/desktop-full.png, 'Onboarding completion, by segment' legend versus the Self-serve Mobile web bar.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Removes the country cut on an invented premise, telling the reader every country segment is under 25 trials rather than that per-country counts are unavailable.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: clicked 'Reveal sample caveat' on B served at port 8732; panel reads 'every country segment this week falls under 25 trials'. The brief supplies only the under-25 labeling rule.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The week-28 timeline is exposed to assistive technology with a stronger claim than the visual: its aria-label asserts a within-week downward trend that the supplied week-level figures cannot support.
findings.evidence: B/source/index.html: role="img" aria-label="Mobile web onboarding completion trended down across week 28, with the new required workspace-name step shipping on Tuesday." The visual marks Tuesday only; no daily series is plotted.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The 'What changed' section wastes its strongest real estate: the headline conversion figure leaves a large empty block beneath it and 'Activated trials' is orphaned alone on a second row.
findings.evidence: rv-mine/B/desktop-full.png at 1440x900 — dead space between the 14.2% figure and the Activated trials row.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Country is offered only as a prose caveat, with no control, so the manager cannot inspect the cut the brief lists as available or confirm the sample claim.
findings.evidence: DOM probe on running B found exactly one select on the page, id 'demo-state'; breakdown toggles cover Device, Channel, and Plan intent only.

findings.label: B
findings.description: At 390px the 'Break down by' toggle group wraps so 'Plan intent' sits alone on its own line, and the six-day timeline labels compress to the edges.
findings.evidence: rv-mine/B/mobile-full.png; no horizontal overflow (scrollWidth equals clientWidth at 390px).

findings.label: B
findings.description: The 'Demo state' review control sits in the product header as a prominent primary affordance rather than being tucked out of the reading path.
findings.evidence: rv-mine/B/desktop-full.png, top right; compare A, which collapses its equivalent into a 'Diagnostics' details element at page end.
